title: POC alignment: cadence, access gates, mid-point review & exec readout - Montara Labs
next_steps: Redwood to share access checklist and SSO configuration doc by 2026-06-01
Customer to provide sample workload (5000 monthly inference units) and 3 canonical prompts by 2026-06-03
Schedule mid-point benchmark review week of 2026-06-22, Redwood to propose 3 slots
action_items: Priya Nair - Draft benchmark config (latency p50/p95, cost per 1k tokens, quality eval prompts) - 2026-06-02
Samir Patel - Confirm VPC peering and KMS ownership, share network diagrams - 2026-06-04
Jordan Meyers - Send commercial pilot pricing sheet and reserved capacity options - 2026-06-01
summary: Initial POC alignment focusing on timeline, success criteria, access prerequisites and mid-point/exec readout cadence. Agreed on benchmark metrics (latency, cost, accuracy on canonical prompts), sample workload size (~5k monthly inference units), and next steps for access and scheduling.
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-05-28
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 49 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Luis Ortega (Montara Director of ML), Maya Chen (Platform Eng), Samir Patel (Security)
Links shared: https://redwood.app/poc-checklist , https://redwood.app/benchmark-template , Montara internal doc: drive.company/montara/poc-sample

[00:00] Jordan Meyers: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we have about 45 minutes, maybe 50, happy to run through a proposed POC cadence and make sure the success criteria line up. Priya and I will be the technical leads from our side.

[00:15] Luis Ortega: Great, thanks Jordan. Quick intro from our side — I'm Luis, I run the ML org, Maya is on platform, and Samir handles infra security. We're trying to validate inference economics and whether we can move from our current transformer-hosted infra to Redwood for low-latency features.

[00:32] Priya Nair: Awesome. High-level goals for the POC we usually see are threefold: 1) functional parity on your prompt set, 2) latency and throughput targets, and 3) unit-cost visibility. Want to confirm which of those are must-haves for you.

[00:48] Maya Chen: The must-have is latency under 200ms p50 for our short prompt path; p95 we'd like under 500ms ideally. Cost is secondary but needs to be demonstrably cheaper per token than our current infra. Also security — VPC and KMS controls are required.

[01:10] Samir Patel: On security we need SOC2 alignment, audit logs for requests, and we need to own the KMS. Is that supported in the private deployment?

[01:22] Jordan Meyers: Yes — Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and private control plane. For the POC we can provision a dedicated testing VPC with peering so you maintain network isolation. We'll send the checklist.

[01:39] Luis Ortega: Good. On workload sizing — we estimate the POC workload to be about 5K inference units per month, with peak bursts up to 500 concurrent small requests. Want to validate throughput at that burst and also see autoscaling behavior.

[01:58] Priya Nair: That sounds sensible. For sizing we'll run two benchmark passes: static batching to measure throughput, and a real-time stream test for tail latency. We'll also run our prefix-caching scenario since you mentioned lots of repeated session prompts.

[02:18] Maya Chen: Can you explain prefix caching again? We have some sessions where users send the same conversation starts.

[02:27] Priya Nair: Sure — prefix/KV caching saves computed keys for repeated prefixes so subsequent calls hit the cache and skip compute, cutting both latency and cost. On Redwood runtime we've seen 30-60% token costs savings on conversational workloads with heavy repetition.

[02:50] Samir Patel: How intrusive is that? Any changes needed in our client?

[02:56] Priya Nair: Minimal. We use the same API surface; we'll provide a reference SDK snippet. You do need to opt in and we need to coordinate cache TTLs. We'll include that in the access checklist.

[03:12] Jordan Meyers: Ok, timeline suggestion: Week 0 (this week) — kickoff and access; Week 1 — access configured and validate connectivity; Week 2-3 — run baseline benchmarks and initial tuning; Week 4 — midpoint readout with performance and cost metrics; Week 5 — run any additional optimizations and exec readout prep; Week 6 — exec readout. Does that fit your internal cadence?

[03:36] Luis Ortega: That seems compressed but doable. We have a VP review that occurs on the 6th week, so aligning the exec readout to that timing works. Can we ensure the midpoint delivers a clear pass/fail gate?

[03:48] Priya Nair: Absolutely. We propose the following gates for midpoint: p50 < 200ms, p95 < 600ms (allowing some buffer), and cost per 1k tokens less than X% of your current baseline — we'll compute that once you share current cost numbers. Also quality threshold — 85% accuracy on the canonical prompt set as measured by your eval rubric.

[04:14] Maya Chen: On the quality metric, we have 120 canonical prompts we've used internally. Would you prefer we give you a subset?

[04:23] Priya Nair: A subset of 20-30 canonical prompts for the POC is ideal — it keeps the runs fast while representative. We'll ask for categories: short queries, multi-turn, and long-form.

[04:38] Jordan Meyers: Action item: Luis to send the canonical prompt subset and current cost-per-1k tokens metric. Samir to confirm who will hold KMS keys and provide a network diagram. Priya will draft the benchmark config.

[04:50] Luis Ortega: We'll get that to you. Question: what mode will you run the POC in — hosted vs dedicated vs private? We need clarity on data residency and contracts.

[05:03] Jordan Meyers: For this POC we recommend Redwood Dedicated with an option to simulate private networking. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and the SLA we need. If you require customer-managed KMS and on-prem, we can move to Private, but that usually lengthens timeline and requires legal. For the POC we can do dedicated with encrypted transit and KMS integration for keys.

[05:28] Samir Patel: If we do dedicated, can we still own the KMS keys?

[05:33] Priya Nair: Yes, we integrate with your KMS via customer-supplied keys; you control rotations. We'll produce an architecture diagram.

[05:44] Maya Chen: Network egress — will traffic stay in our VPC? How do you handle peering?

[05:51] Priya Nair: We can either do VPC peering or private link; peering is straightforward for quick POCs. We'll detail TCP/IP ranges and firewall rules in the checklist.

[06:05] Jordan Meyers: Let's talk benchmarks briefly. We'll run three profiles: 1) latency profile using short prompts to measure p50/p95 and jitter; 2) throughput profile with batching, measuring tokens/sec; and 3) regression quality check across canonical prompts with human or automated scoring. Any other metrics you want surfaced?

[06:29] Luis Ortega: Error rates and retry behavior are important — we need to ensure graceful degradation. Also tokenized cost breakdown per-call so we can see cost attribution per route.

[06:40] Priya Nair: We'll enable token-level cost breakdown in the console and provide a cost export CSV. For error and retry, we'll run synthetic spike tests to observe fallback to model variants or queueing behavior.

[06:56] Samir Patel: On compliance, our legal team will need SOC2 artifacts and the audit log retention period. How long do you retain logs for the Dedicated POC by default?

[07:06] Jordan Meyers: Default is 90 days for logs, but for Dedicated we can extend retention as an add-on. We'll send SOC2 and audit doc references with expected redactions for POC.

[07:20] Maya Chen: About benchmark environment — do you need docker images from us or sample data?

[07:26] Priya Nair: Prefer sample anonymized payloads and the prompt subset. No need for full data. If there are large artifacts we can pull via a signed S3 link.

[07:36] Luis Ortega: We will provide anonymized examples. Also we have some edge cases with long context windows — can you run tests up to 8k tokens?

[07:44] Priya Nair: Yes, we can run up to 8k. For very long contexts we may recommend quantized model variants to lower memory usage; we'll include model/quantization recommendations in the readout.

[07:59] Jordan Meyers: Ok, planning notes: we'll create a shared spreadsheet with benchmark steps, configuration, and expected results. Priya will own test execution, Luis will validate results, Samir will sign off on security gating, Jordan will coordinate commercial readout.

[08:14] Maya Chen: For the mid-point review, what deliverables will we get?

[08:19] Priya Nair: Midpoint will include: benchmark CSVs with latency and throughput numbers, cost per token analysis, short notes on tuning done (batching, cache TTL), and an initial quality report on the canonical prompts. We'll also show a quick demo of the live run.

[08:35] Luis Ortega: And for exec readout?

[08:37] Jordan Meyers: Exec readout will be a 30-minute slide deck with a one-page summary: pass/fail on gates, TCO comparison, risks & mitigations, and recommended next steps (go-forward path, reserved capacity commitment options).

[08:52] Samir Patel: On legal, roughly how long for an enterprise contract if we proceed after POC?

[08:57] Jordan Meyers: Typically 4-8 weeks depending on e-signature and standard SOW; if there's custom on-prem work it can extend. We can provide a draft SOW early to parallelize legal review.

[09:10] Maya Chen: Can we capture a rough estimate of cost improvement you'd target to consider adoption?

[09:15] Jordan Meyers: From past similar customers, we aim for 20-40% lower per-token cost leveraging caching and quantized variants plus lower infra overhead. We'll be specific once we see your baseline.

[09:29] Luis Ortega: Good. One more ops question — will the POC include tracing hooks so our app logs can correlate requests to model responses?

[09:38] Priya Nair: Yes, we support trace IDs and headers. We'll give you an instrumentation snippet and tracing dashboard access for the duration of the POC.

[09:49] Jordan Meyers: Let's confirm the concrete schedule and owners now: Kickoff (today) — access checklist out by 6/1. Access provisioning — target 6/5. Baseline benchmarks complete — target 6/12. Midpoint readout — week of 6/22. Exec readout — week of 7/6 to align with your VP review. Does that sound ok?

[10:08] Luis Ortega: Yes, those dates align with internal timelines. We'll block the mid-point and exec slots offline.

[10:15] Samir Patel: For the access checklist, we need to review the SSO/SAML flow. Do you support provisioning via SCIM?

[10:22] Priya Nair: We do — SCIM and SAML supported. We'll include the SSO/SCIM setup guide in the checklist.

[10:29] Maya Chen: Any infrastructure limits we should know about for Dedicated POC?

[10:33] Priya Nair: We typically provision a predictable GPU pool. For your 500 concurrent small requests estimate we'll size for that with autoscaling burst headroom. If you need deterministic tail latency at large scale we recommend reserved capacity.

[10:49] Luis Ortega: Noted. Can we also get a rough runbook for failure modes during tests?

[10:55] Jordan Meyers: Yes, we'll share a runbook that includes steps for network failures, KMS key rotation, model fallback policies, and when to escalate to SE.

[11:05] (crosstalk)

[11:12] Priya Nair: Quick tech detail — for the benchmark config I'll propose two kernel/quantization picks: one high-perf int8 path and one conservative fp16 path so you can compare quality vs cost.

[11:26] Luis Ortega: Perfect. On the quality rubric — we'll send how we score outputs (0-3 scale). Will Redwood accept that scoring format?

[11:33] Priya Nair: Yes, we'll ingest your rubric. If you can provide samples scored by your SMEs, we can calibrate the automated checks.

[11:44] Jordan Meyers: Anything else we should capture?

[11:47] Maya Chen: One small ask — can we have a short runbook for installing the Redwood SDK in our CI? We need to instrument nightly regression runs.

[11:56] Priya Nair: We'll provide a CI example and a GitHub Actions snippet.

[12:03] Luis Ortega: Great. Ok last part — risk assessment. We're concerned about model drift and long-term maintenance. How does Redwood handle model upgrades in production?

[12:15] Jordan Meyers: We support pinned model versions and staged rollouts (canary/A-B). Also automatic rollback if quality regressions are detected against your eval sets. Redwood Optimize can flag regressions and trigger alerts.

[12:30] Samir Patel: If we detect a regression during POC, what's the remediation SLA?

[12:36] Priya Nair: For POC we commit to troubleshooting within 24 business hours and a hotfix path typically within 3 business days. For Dedicated enterprise contracts we have SLA clauses.

[12:48] (brief pause)

[13:00] Jordan Meyers: Alright let's recap real quick. Deliverables: access checklist + SSO guide (Jordan), benchmark config and execution plan (Priya), canonical prompt subset and cost baseline (Luis), network/KMS diagram (Samir). Midpoint readout week of 6/22; exec readout aligned to week of 7/6.

[13:22] Luis Ortega: Sounds good. We'll aim to have the canonical set and cost numbers by 6/3.

[13:29] Maya Chen: We will also confirm peering details by 6/4.

[13:33] Jordan Meyers: Perfect. I'll send meeting notes and the checklist within 24 hours. Priya, want to add anything?

[13:40] Priya Nair: Just that we'll include example results for caching and a small script to reproduce runs locally. Expect the benchmark template link and a sample CSV from us.

[13:52] Samir Patel: Ok thanks everyone. Looking forward.

[13:56] Jordan Meyers: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the artifacts and proposed mid-point slots.

[14:02] Recording ends.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings — e.g., "replicate" appears as lowercase and some acronyms like "KMS" get spelled out inconsistently. Speakers labeled with names for clarity though Fireflies export sometimes uses Speaker 1/Speaker 2.
